name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: French 10-year yield eased to 4.74% on 26 Nov, near a two-month low, after October's 24-year high; no failed G7 auction
state: The French 10-year yield was little changed at 4.74% on 26 Nov, close to its lowest since late September, after a global bond rally on 25 Nov (Trading Economics). It climbed towards 4.9% on 13 Nov as markets priced ECB rate rises and peaked at a 24-year high above 5% in October. No confirmed France–Bund spread above 150bp, failed G7 auction or emergency central-bank buying was found as of 27 Nov, so Watch holds on still-elevated long-dated yields.
for_you: Governments facing higher borrowing costs tend to tighten budgets, which can affect public services and taxes. Mortgage and loan rates in France and elsewhere in Europe tend to follow government bond yields.
rubric_hit: Watch: G7 long-dated yields near multi-decade highs (French 10y 24-year high in Oct); no failed auction or France–Bund > 150bp

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
